answer.rationale: With the incumbent refusing to reopen price and finance mandating an 18% spend cut, renewing at existing terms cannot meet the objective. memory_c2 documents a proven, low-risk switch: the low-cost vendor was onboarded quickly, invoicing was accurate, and unit cost dropped sharply. memory_c4 confirms that renegotiation only works when the incumbent is willing to move on price/terms; given the explicit refusal this cycle, that lever is exhausted. Switching primary supply to the established low-cost vendor is the single action that directly attacks the cost mandate without introducing the lead-time risk of qualifying a brand-new source. The 14-day window before expiry is tight but aligns with the quick-onboarding history in c2. Delivery risk is held in check because the assembly line is at 94% committed volume with no buffer; a proven vendor with accurate invoicing and prior fast onboarding is the lowest-risk path to the cost target within the one-decision constraint.
